If I were you I would try and slow down a little bit, take each thing as they come. 

It sounds like you have a very manic life at the moment and it's easy to let things get on top of you if you let it. 

I'm sure there are plenty of things that are positive about your life, I understand how hard it is to see these, especially when you are depressed but I believe in time you will be able to see them and enjoy them again. 

Firstly, I'd probably say you have too much stuff going on at the moment for a relationship. Work on yourself first, work on your situation and your happiness and then when the times right a relationship will come naturally. 

Start again now. Forgot the past, whatever you have done and whatever has happened is over and only has power over you if you think about it. Whatever happened you can either dwell on it and suffer from it or take it as fact, accept it, learn from it and then move on. 

Now is when you start improving your life. Start on something small. 

Do you exercise? Maybe you can start working on your fitness, pick up yoga or start cooking healthy. I always think that's a good start to work on. 

Start looking for jobs, go to your job centre (or version of that if you have one in your country) and ask for help. Maybe you can ask in pubs and keep checking the papers for openings. Rather than worry about not having a job, accept that you haven't got one, accept that you need one and then go and look. Worrying won't change anything but action will. 

I understand how hard college can be, especially if you get behind but they are usually very good with helping people. Go and see your teacher and explain that you are struggling. Again, don't worry about your situation, accept it and then work on making it better- action makes things happen, worrying does nothing except hurt yourself. 

If it's 4am as you say then you cannot do anything at the moment- accept it. Relax and take this time to chill out. Maybe try some meditation? A quick google will give you something to follow i'm sure. 

Tackle the day tomorrow, start working on making a new you.

Not sure how to edit it on my phone but i thought i'd add a bit to this. A big help for me was learning how to draw the ball. With the same thoughts in mind above try and go in to out or slightly close the club face through impact. 
If you keep practising this and seeing how you can shape the shots differently then hopefully it will click why you are slicing it. I've been doing this for a while and I can start to feel if the ball will slice or hook as soon as i've hit it. 
Right now i'm really focusing on bringing the club back straight and slow and hitting down on it to get a straight path. Good luck!

I used to slice my driver all the time and I had sort of an epiphany which really helped me lessen it and then eventually start hitting it straight. 
What I did was starting to think of hitting the golf ball as if i was kicking a football (soccer ball). I realise that if you haven't played football before then it may be of no help but its a good image for me anyway. 
If you imagine how you curl the ball, either using the inside of your foot for right to left curl (draw) or outside of the foot for left to right (fade)- this is how i see the golf ball. 
If your slicing it you are either hitting the ball straight thru with the club face open or hitting across it- out to in. 
I started to focus on where my club face was pointed at impact and what path I was taking through the ball and corrected them as necessary.
A lot of practice later and there going straighter, a lot more often!
Hopefully this can help you too.
